claims.text: Placing graphene nanoplatelets at W–Cu interfaces will increase the composite's overall thermal conductivity.
Adding interfacial graphene nanoplatelets will not sacrifice the mechanical durability of the W–Cu composite.
Adding interfacial graphene nanoplatelets will not sacrifice the irradiation resistance of the W–Cu composite.
Pre-coating or uniformly mixing graphene nanoplatelets with W and/or Cu powders before consolidation will produce a thin graphene layer between W and Cu regions.
A graphene interlayer at W–Cu interfaces enhances heat-transfer pathways.
A graphene interlayer at W–Cu interfaces improves interfacial bonding.
Graphene has intrinsically high in-plane thermal conductivity.
Thermal contact at an unmodified tungsten–copper interface is typically imperfect.
Graphene bridges imperfect thermal contact at W–Cu interfaces and thereby accelerates overall heat dissipation.
Graphene has excellent mechanical strength.
Graphene has excellent irradiation stability.
Graphene's mechanical properties help maintain the structural integrity of a W–Cu composite.
Graphene helps a W–Cu composite resist radiation-induced damage.
The graphene-modified W–Cu composite will have higher thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable graphene-free W–Cu composite.
The graphene-modified W–Cu composite will retain mechanical durability comparable to the graphene-free baseline.
The graphene-modified W–Cu composite will retain irradiation resistance comparable to the graphene-free baseline.
Keeping the graphene fraction low and uniform will avoid percolation or agglomeration problems.
The predicted improvement will persist at reactor-relevant temperatures and irradiation doses if processing produces a clean, well-bonded interface.
The optimal graphene loading, dispersion, and long-term irradiation stability of the graphene–metal interface are not yet known.
Failure to increase thermal conductivity, or degradation of mechanical properties or irradiation resistance relative to the control, would falsify the hypothesis.
